title: Notable recent biology and biomedical papers from the 2026-11-16 arXiv announcement batch
global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart. This is a relevance-ranked inference from incomplete biomedical coverage, not a popularity ranking, systematic review, or clinical evidence assessment. Much clinical and experimental biology research appears on bioRxiv or medRxiv instead.

sections.title: Headline
sections.summary: The latest available batch is Monday, 16 November 2026, with 7 new submissions and 4 cross-listings. Protein-function and molecular-structure evaluation are prominent, alongside transcriptomics prediction and biomedical imaging. Snapshot 2026-11-17T01:26:49Z uses the prior batch because the 17 November announcement had not yet occurred; attention evidence is too sparse for a popularity ranking.

sections.title: Confident and Wrong: Structure Confidence Is a Poor Selection Filter for Protein Function
sections.abstract: The authors compare three lanmodulin design strategies and report that function-guided selection yielded substantially more terbium-binding variants than selection by structural-confidence scores.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report 83.3% terbium binding in the function-guided panel versus 16.7% in the structure-confidence-selected panel, arguing that measured-function supervision was a better selection signal for this design task.
sections.unique_caveat: The comparison is bounded to lanmodulin rare-earth binding; the design panels also differed in generative method, so the result does not establish that structural confidence fails for other proteins or tasks.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: New q-bio.BM submission; 297 designs were screened against terbium and dysprosium using biochemical binding assays, the most direct functional experiment in this set.

sections.title: CARVE: A glycan-specific framework for assessing protein-glycan binding-pose quality
sections.abstract: CARVE combines glycan-aware geometry and contact measures to classify predicted protein–glycan poses, then benchmarks nine methods on experimentally determined complexes.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report that HADDOCK3 reached the highest Acceptable-level success rate among top-25 predictions per target (47%); no tested method exceeded 20% for high-quality, structurally valid poses.
sections.unique_caveat: This is a benchmark of predicted structures against existing complexes, not prospective experimental validation of new binding. The temporal split reduces possible training overlap but does not establish that every benchmark structure was unseen by every prediction method.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: New q-bio.BM submission; CARVE-Score reproduced quality classes on 25,068 poses (macro-F1 0.892), while CARVE-Bench covers 1,974 complexes and nine prediction methods.

sections.title: Scan-specific k-space interpolation using deep Koopman autoencoders
sections.abstract: A scan-specific deep Koopman autoencoder reconstructs retrospectively undersampled brain MRI k-space data and is compared with GRAPPA and RAKI.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report better reconstruction metrics than GRAPPA and RAKI and reader preference over RAKI, with improved ratings for sharpness, aliasing, and overall image quality.
sections.unique_caveat: Evaluation used retrospective brain scans from one dataset; the authors call for tests on other anatomies, scanners, and coils. Reader preference is not evidence of improved clinical outcomes.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: New primary submission in medical physics; tested on 281 retrospectively undersampled brain datasets and a 52-image reader-study subset.

sections.title: S1Pert: Scalable Target-Specific Gene Response Prediction with System-One Intelligence
sections.abstract: S1Pert combines uncertainty-aware response labels, reusable target and gene representations, and a hierarchical decoder to predict transcriptional responses to unseen genetic perturbations.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors present an inference-efficient framework intended to distinguish perturbation-specific responses rather than relying on historical gene-level response frequencies.
sections.unique_caveat: This is computational evaluation on existing perturbation data, not prospective CRISPR validation; response labels and performance remain dependent on the benchmark and cell context.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: New genomics submission; the authors evaluate target-specific response discrimination across multiple cellular contexts and report improved performance over baselines.

sections.title: More Genes, Faster Inference: Efficient Large-Panel Spatial Transcriptomics Prediction from Histology
sections.abstract: GeneFlow combines tissue-image morphology and spatial gene interactions to predict large-panel spatial expression directly from histology.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors describe a flow-matching model that predicts spatial gene-expression profiles from histology while reducing computational cost.
sections.unique_caveat: Expression is computationally inferred from images; benchmark performance does not establish that predicted profiles substitute for measured spatial transcriptomics or transfer to new tissue types and sites.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The authors report benchmark comparisons across multiple spatial-transcriptomics datasets, including up to 56.8% gains for 1,000-gene prediction.

sections.title: Deciphering multiple binding modes in large protein complexes via Enhanced Sampling and beta-VAE: the CYFIP1-eIF4E case
sections.abstract: Enhanced molecular sampling and latent-space clustering are used to propose three binding modes for the flexible CYFIP1–eIF4E protein complex.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors’ simulations suggest CYFIP1 samples the canonical dorsal site, a non-canonical lateral site, and a combined mode on eIF4E, including contacts outside the previously emphasized interface.
sections.unique_caveat: The proposed interface modes are computational. Coarse-graining and elastic-network restraints limit side-chain detail and large-scale motion; experimental binding or mutagenesis tests remain necessary.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The analysis uses ten enhanced-sampling replicas totaling 100 μs to identify recurring interface modes.

sections.title: Exact stochastic theory of post-transcriptional gene autoregulation mediated by RNA-binding proteins
sections.abstract: An analytical stochastic model derives protein-number and burst-size distributions for RNA-binding-protein-mediated feedback and compares predicted noise and rhythm transmission with transcriptional feedback.
sections.claimed_contribution: The author derives a steady-state distribution and a criterion for sub-Poissonian fluctuations, and predicts different noise-suppression advantages for positive versus negative feedback.
sections.unique_caveat: These are theoretical results from a reaction model, not newly measured molecular or cellular effects; the predicted regime differences need experimental testing.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: New q-bio.MN submission, cross-listed in biological physics and statistical mechanics; it gives an exact mathematical treatment of a molecular feedback mechanism.

sections.title: Certificate-Based Verification of Pulsed Field Ablation Models
sections.abstract: The paper proposes independent mathematical certificates that bound numerical error in pulsed-field-ablation simulations of electric fields and lesion maps.
sections.claimed_contribution: For a modeled focal electrode, the authors certify lesion-depth bounds of 3.50–3.75 mm at specified voltage and field thresholds across a stated conductivity-ratio range.
sections.unique_caveat: The certificates assess whether a specified mathematical model was solved within bounds; they do not validate the model’s tissue assumptions, lethal-field threshold, or predicted lesion against biological measurements.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The authors compare certificate-based bounds with grid-convergence studies and report a checker running at roughly one-tenth of solve time.

sections.title: A thorough review on Deep Learning approaches to 2D-to-3D Registration in Medical Imaging
sections.abstract: This review compares deep-learning approaches to 2D-to-3D registration across 41 studies, emphasizing pipeline design, metrics, and domain adaptation.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors identify per-case uncertainty estimation and temporal/sequential modeling as under-addressed issues for clinical readiness.
sections.unique_caveat: This is a review of published methods, not a new comparative clinical study; conclusions depend on the coverage and evaluation choices of the included papers.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The review synthesizes 41 studies and reports that 23 use direct regression and 18 iterative pipelines, with X-ray-to-CT work dominating the reviewed literature.

sections.title: Domain-repetition patterns in protein domain trigrams are uniform across chromosomes and conserved among multicellular eukaryotes
sections.abstract: A reproducible analysis of Pfam domain triplets across 16 organisms reports broadly similar repetition-pattern proportions across chromosomes and multicellular eukaryotes.
sections.claimed_contribution: The author reports conserved proportions of distinct three-domain patterns among multicellular eukaryotes, with chromosome-level exceptions including KRAB zinc-finger-rich regions.
sections.unique_caveat: This is a computational proteome-pattern analysis; the reported distributions do not establish functional consequences or causal evolutionary mechanisms.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The analysis covers 199 chromosomes or other proteome components across 14 organisms and compares distinct domain triplets using gene-level permutations.

sections.title: Emergent intercellular contact-force networks shaped by deformability
sections.abstract: Cell-based simulations report that deformability and local geometry organize force networks in dense assemblies of active cells.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report a bimodal contact-force distribution and a characteristic weak-tip/strong-side network motif in a modeled soft-liquid regime, dependent on cell deformability.
sections.unique_caveat: The findings are simulation-based and depend on the Fourier Contour Cell model and assumptions about deformability and active motility; they are not direct observations of tissue forces.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The authors compare deformable and non-deformable simulations and use persistent-homology analysis to characterize force-network structure.

sections.title: Trending Research Themes
sections.summary: Within the selected batch: protein-function and molecular-structure evaluation (Confident and Wrong, CARVE, CYFIP1–eIF4E); gene-expression prediction (S1Pert, GeneFlow); computational mechanism models for RNA feedback and cell force networks; and medical imaging or model verification (MRI, registration review, pulsed-field ablation). The evidence and validation types differ; these do not establish field-wide shifts.

sections.title: Open Problems and Research Directions
sections.summary: Proposed follow-ups include testing function-guided selection across protein folds, auditing glycan benchmark exposure and validating poses experimentally, external replication of transcriptomic predictions, testing molecular simulation and RNA-feedback predictions experimentally, and evaluating MRI and ablation models across sites and against physical measurements.

sections.title: Takeaway
sections.summary: The clearest direct biological experiment is a bounded lanmodulin design comparison; CARVE provides a broad glycan benchmark, while other papers contribute transcriptomic prediction, molecular simulation, RNA theory, and imaging or model-verification methods. This is a relevance-ranked snapshot, not a popularity chart or clinical evidence assessment.
